name: OPM Structured Interview Guide and resources
what: The U.S. Office of Personnel Management's definition of a [structured interview](#term:structured-interview) (same predetermined questions in the same order, scored on the same rating scale; behavioural and situational question types) with a linked Structured Interview Guide, a presentation, a webcast, a training video and a sample question with rating scale [41](#cite:41).
conditions: written for federal hiring; usable by any employer (synthesis)

name: Google re:Work guide to structured interviewing
what: A large employer's published template: four components (vetted questions, full feedback recording, standardised rubrics with poor/borderline/solid/outstanding anchors, interviewer training and calibration), attributes in three areas, and company-reported results stated without methods (about 40 minutes saved per interview; rejected candidates 35 percent happier) [42](#cite:42).
conditions: a practitioner template, not evidence of effect; the figures are the company's own claims [42](#cite:42)

name: SIOP Principles for the Validation and Use of Personnel Selection Procedures (5th ed.)
what: The profession's standard for validating and using selection procedures, consistent with the 2014 Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing and adopted as official APA policy in August 2018; 97 pages [29](#cite:29).
cost: published in Industrial and Organizational Psychology 11(S1); access terms as the publisher sets them [29](#cite:29)
conditions: what "professionally developed" means when a validation study is challenged (synthesis from [29](#cite:29) [32](#cite:32))

name: QIC-WD umbrella summaries (work sample tests; realistic job previews)
what: Government-funded plain-language summaries of the [meta-analytic](#term:meta-analysis) evidence on selection tools, with the practical conditions: build from a [job analysis](#term:job-analysis), standardise administration and scoring, use [work samples](#term:work-sample-test) for untrained prerequisites, and get expert help [17](#cite:17).
conditions: written for public child-welfare agencies; the evidence base is general [17](#cite:17)

name: ISO 30405:2023 Guidelines on recruitment
what: The international recruitment guideline, organised into preparing and planning, attracting, sourcing, assessing, decision-making and pre-boarding, with a cost-and-effectiveness section; second edition, June 2023 [45](#cite:45). Companion technical specifications define [cost per hire](#term:cost-per-hire) (ISO/[TS](#term:top-secret) 30407), impact of hire (30410) and quality of hire (30411) [46](#cite:46).
cost: purchased from ISO or a national body; the preview is free [45](#cite:45)
conditions: definitions to cite for the indicators file; the body was not read [45](#cite:45) [46](#cite:46)

name: DOJ Civil Rights Division employer fact sheet on export controls and immigration-related discrimination
what: The Immigrant and Employee Rights Section's fact sheet (rev. March 2024): [U.S. persons](#term:us-person) are citizens, nationals, permanent residents, refugees and asylees; do not tell applicants the export rules require a citizenship; assess only the positions that work with controlled items; keep the assessment separate from [Form I-9](#term:form-i-9) and do not limit document choice; apply to State or Commerce for authorization for a non-U.S. person [131](#cite:131). Read in sweep 1 through a law-firm summary [51](#cite:51); the primary was read in sweep 4.
conditions: none; the fact sheet is guidance, with the enforcement record behind it [49](#cite:49) [50](#cite:50)

name: DoD SkillBridge
what: Transitioning service members train with an industry partner during their last 180 days under a memorandum of understanding; the partner commits to a minimum annual intake by size (one participant for employers of 200 or fewer) and to a 75 percent qualifying-offer rate on completion, with an 85 percent goal, plus liaison, incident reporting and outcome data at 90 and 180 days [74](#cite:74).
cost: no wage cost during the internship, as the law-firm summary states it; the service continues pay and benefits [59](#cite:59)
conditions: the MOU terms above; a 2023 application pause and Navy and Marine Corps rank-based limits were reported [59](#cite:59)

pending_changes.text: August 2024 MOU release introduced the minimum-intake and 75% offer-rate obligations [74](#cite:74) [59](#cite:59).

name: Hiring Our Heroes fellowships (U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation)
what: A twelve-week Corporate Fellowship Program giving transitioning service members training and civilian workplace experience, a [Skills-Based](#term:skills-based-hiring) Fellowship open to service members and military spouses, and a Military Spouse Professional Network [83](#cite:83).
cost: not stated on the page read (todo)
conditions: eligibility, pay status and employer obligations not stated on the page read (todo)

name: State workforce agency job banks (employment service delivery system)
what: The public job banks with which a covered federal contractor must list every opening, concurrently with other recruiting, and which then give priority [referral](#term:referral-hiring) of [protected veterans](#term:vevraa) [73](#cite:73).
conditions: mandatory for covered contractors; open to any employer (synthesis)

name: Handshake (campus recruiting platform)
what: A university career-services platform used for early-career recruiting; listed here as the tooling category's example, to be described as the vendor states it in sweep 8. The 2026 campus benchmark is a planned 5.6 percent increase in graduate hiring [79](#cite:79).
conditions: postings must avoid the listed ADEA age terms [78](#cite:78)

name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS)
what: Annual wage and employment estimates by occupation, nationally and by metropolitan area; May 2025 estimates published May 15, 2026 (software developers: median \$65.38 per hour, mean \$148,100 a year) [110](#cite:110). The series the [Service Contract Act](#term:service-contract-act) [wage determinations](#term:wage-determination) are generally built from [101](#cite:101).
conditions: use the metro-area table for the SOC code; the refresh routine should pull by series (todo)

name: BLS Employment Cost Index (ECI)
what: Quarterly index of wages and benefits; private-industry wages rose 3.1 percent and benefits 3.8 percent in the year to June 2026 [103](#cite:103). The index the OFPP [compensation cap](#term:compensation-cap) and many price-adjustment clauses use [107](#cite:107).
conditions: quarterly; the market-escalation evidence for a rate request (synthesis)

name: BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation (ECEC)
what: Quarterly cost per hour worked for wages and each benefit; benefits were 30.0 percent of private-industry compensation in June 2026, 31.5 percent for management and professional occupations [104](#cite:104).
conditions: the benefits share for a total-rewards statement (synthesis)

name: GSA CALC+ labor ceiling rates
what: Awarded ceiling hourly rates by [labor category](#term:labor-category) from GSA Multiple Award Schedule contracts, filterable by education, experience, worksite, business size and [security clearance](#term:security-clearance); no credentials required; user guide version 2.0, June 24, 2026 [111](#cite:111).
conditions: ceiling rates, not paid salaries; the wrap-rate arithmetic converts them (synthesis)

name: KFF Employer Health Benefits Survey
what: Annual survey of employer premiums, contributions and offer rates; 2025: family premium \$26,993, worker share \$6,850, offer rate 59 percent at 10–199 workers [105](#cite:105).
conditions: the dollar figure for the largest benefit line (synthesis)

name: ClearanceJobs Compensation Report (annual)
what: Vendor survey of [cleared professionals](#term:cleared-population)' pay by [clearance](#term:security-clearance) level, [polygraph](#term:polygraph), employer type and location; 2025 edition: 13,177 responses, average \$119,131, [Secret](#term:secret) \$100,296, [Top Secret](#term:top-secret) \$124,084, [TS/SCI](#term:sensitive-compartmented-information) \$132,177 [89](#cite:89).
conditions: self-selected respondents on one job board; the premium ladder, not a census (synthesis)

name: SAM.gov wage determinations (Service Contract Act)
what: The [wage determinations](#term:wage-determination) agencies attach to service contracts, by locality and occupation, with the [SCA](#term:service-contract-act) Directory of Occupations for classification; the [H&W rate](#term:health-and-welfare-rate) \$5.55 from July 2025 [101](#cite:101).
conditions: floors for covered service employees; conformance for unlisted classes [101](#cite:101)

name: DCSA personnel-vetting systems (DISS, NBIS and eApp, SWFT)
what: The government systems a facility security officer uses to [sponsor](#term:clearance-sponsorship) and track a hire: the system that shows investigations and personnel security determinations, the [end-to-end](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) personnel vetting system with its [electronic questionnaire](#term:eapp), and fingerprint transmission to the FBI, as [DCSA](#term:dcsa) describes them [149](#cite:149); named in the sponsorship roadmap as [DISS](#term:diss) and e-QIP [146](#cite:146) and on the [NBIS roadmap](#term:nbis) as DISS-JVS, eApp and the Individual Engagement Platform with milestones through FY2028 [125](#cite:125).
cost: free to the contractor; the government funds investigation processing [146](#cite:146)
conditions: access through the firm's cleared FSO; account provisioning by DCSA (synthesis)

pending_changes.text: eVetting for low and moderate tiers FY27 Q4; [TW 2.0](#term:trusted-workforce-2) full operating capability FY28 Q1 [125](#cite:125)

name: National Industrial Security System (NISS)
what: [DCSA](#term:dcsa)'s system of record for industrial security oversight [149](#cite:149), where a [sponsor](#term:clearance-sponsorship) submits a facility-clearance sponsorship and the firm uploads its [FCL](#term:facility-clearance) package, with the package review at day 20 and the key officials' submissions due by day 45 [146](#cite:146).
conditions: a sponsor with a bona fide need must open the request; the firm cannot [146](#cite:146) [120](#cite:120)

name: DCSA roadmap to getting a facility clearance
what: The [Facility Clearance](#term:facility-clearance) Branch's own walk-through: [sponsorship](#term:clearance-sponsorship) by a contracting activity or a [cleared](#term:security-clearance) [prime](#term:prime-contractor), the pre-award and post-award documents, the NISS steps on a day-by-day clock, the key officials who must be cleared, and the reasons packages are rejected [146](#cite:146).
conditions: June 2022 presentation; check DCSA for updated submission procedures (todo)

name: NISPPAC public meeting slides (industry clearance timeliness)
what: The advisory committee meetings at which [DCSA](#term:dcsa) reports industry [inventory](#term:investigation-inventory) and [timeliness](#term:end-to-end-timeliness) by phase, DHS and DOE report their contractor figures, and the [NBIS roadmap](#term:nbis) is updated; slides are posted by the Information Security Oversight Office [125](#cite:125). Vendor summaries restate the DCSA figures within days [124](#cite:124) [126](#cite:126).
conditions: figures arrive months after the quarter and the reporting basis changed in FY2026 Q3 [126](#cite:126) [127](#cite:127)

name: USCIS I-9 Central and the Handbook for Employers (M-274)
what: The government's own instructions for [Form I-9](#term:form-i-9): who completes which section by when, the acceptable documents the employee chooses among, receipts, the remote alternative for [E-Verify](#term:e-verify) employers, reverification and retention [130](#cite:130).
conditions: none

name: FTC guidance, Using consumer reports: what employers need to know
what: The regulator's plain statement of the disclosure, permission, certification and two-notice sequence a [background check](#term:consumer-report) requires, with the extra duties for investigative reports and a pointer to state restrictions on [credit reports](#term:credit-check-law) [136](#cite:136).
conditions: federal floor; state law may add waiting periods and limits (todo)

name: DoD Manual 8140.03 (cyberspace workforce qualification)
what: The manual that sets the foundational, resident and continuing-development qualifications for each cyberspace work role and requires contracted support to hold the [foundational qualification](#term:dod-8140) on commencement [139](#cite:139).
cost: free; certifications and training are the hire's or the firm's cost (synthesis)
conditions: the contract names the work roles and any resident requirements [139](#cite:139)

name: QIC-WD umbrella summaries (organizational socialization; training transfer; job embeddedness)
what: Plain-language federal summaries of the [onboarding](#term:onboarding), transfer and [embeddedness](#term:job-embeddedness) [meta-analyses](#term:meta-analysis) with the practices they support: job shadowing, insiders as guides, consistent feedback, [mentoring](#term:mentoring) and affirming [newcomers](#term:newcomer-adjustment)' identities [154](#cite:154); cueing, previews, voluntary participation, hands-on practice and feedback for transfer, with the open- versus closed-skill distinction [163](#cite:163); links, fit and sacrifice on and off the job, with on-the-job embeddedness the more predictive and the suggested practices untested [192](#cite:192).
conditions: written for public child-welfare agencies; the effect sizes are in the primaries [152](#cite:152) [162](#cite:162) [178](#cite:178)

name: Registered Apprenticeship (U.S. Department of Labor and state agencies)
what: Paid work with related instruction and [mentoring](#term:mentoring) under registered standards; the employer hub offers a standards builder, a partner finder and pre-apprenticeship links, and a program can be approved for GI Bill benefits through a State Approving Agency [177](#cite:177). About 940,000 participants in FY2024, computer occupations third at 7 percent; smaller employers report registration and reporting burden and cost [172](#cite:172).
cost: apprentice wages (median starting wage \$19/hour FY2024), instruction, registration and reporting; DOL grants fund about 3% of participants [172](#cite:172)
conditions: registered standards; progress reporting; a mentor; completion rates run about 42% within a year of the expected date [172](#cite:172)

name: IRS section 127 FAQs and sample plan (FS-2026-10; Publication 5993)
what: The revised FAQs on [educational assistance programs](#term:section-127-plan): the \$5,250 limit indexed after 2026, student-loan payments without sunset, the written-plan and notice requirements, and a sample plan document [174](#cite:174).
conditions: separate written plan; nondiscrimination; employee notice [174](#cite:174)

name: Center for Development of Security Excellence (DCSA)
what: The government's security-training school for the DoD and industry security community: learning platforms on changing security policy and procedure, professional development, and certificates or university transfer credit [176](#cite:176). Where a firm's facility security officer and insider-threat official need training for the NISP role, this is the source ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker) from [120](#cite:120)).
cost: not stated on the page read; the FSO curriculum and eLearning catalogue are on inner pages (todo)
conditions: open to the DoD security community; industry access terms not read (todo)

name: DOJ/FTC antitrust guidelines for business activities affecting workers (2025)
what: The agencies' statement of what employers may and may not agree with each other about hiring and pay: [no-poach agreements](#term:no-poach-agreement) are criminal, wage coordination is wage-fixing, [non-solicit terms](#term:non-solicitation-agreement) survive only as collateral and necessary parts of a collaboration, and compensation information sharing is a risk [187](#cite:187).
conditions: in force as of the sweep; replaces the 2016 HR guidance [187](#cite:187)

name: SEAD 3 self-reporting list (agency summary)
what: An agency's plain-language list of what a [clearance](#term:security-clearance) holder must report about foreign travel, foreign contacts, finances, arrests, treatment, cohabitants, outside employment and other individuals, with the five-day travel rule [190](#cite:190).
conditions: the NRC's channel is its own; a contractor reports through its FSO to the cognizant agency [189](#cite:189)

name: DOL plant closings and layoffs page (WARN)
what: The Department's statement of the [WARN](#term:warn-act) thresholds, the 60-day notice and the exceptions [191](#cite:191).
conditions: federal floor; state mini-WARN laws differ (sweep 8)

name: SHRM recruiting benchmarking reports
what: Member-survey medians for [cost-per-hire](#term:cost-per-hire), [time-to-fill](#term:time-to-fill) and [requisitions](#term:requisition) per recruiter by organisation size, with the cost-per-hire components defined [196](#cite:196); the 2025 brief and the State of Recruiting article [43](#cite:43).
cost: free summaries; member access for the full data [196](#cite:196)
conditions: survey of SHRM members; medians, not averages; the year travels with every figure [196](#cite:196)

name: GAO key principles for strategic workforce planning (GAO-04-39)
what: The five principles, involve stakeholders, determine the critical skills, tailor strategies to the gaps, build the capability, monitor and evaluate, and the definition of [strategic workforce planning](#term:workforce-planning) as long-term strategies for acquiring, developing and retaining the workforce [205](#cite:205).
conditions: written for federal agencies in 2003; the principles are general [205](#cite:205)

name: DOT SBIR cost and pricing proposal instructions (rate build-up)
what: A government agency''s plain statement of the [indirect rate](#term:overhead-rate) structure behind a [billing rate](#term:wrap-rate): fringe on labor, overhead on labor and fringe, [G&A](#term:general-and-administrative-rate) on total cost input, profit as a rate, with approved rates from [DCAA](#term:dcaa) or the contractor''s own calculations [206](#cite:206).
conditions: 2016 instructions for a Phase I proposal; the structure is general (synthesis)

name: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS)
what: Monthly openings, hires, quits and layoffs by industry; the [openings rate](#term:job-openings-rate) in professional and business services and the [quits rate](#term:quits-rate) are the pack's demand and churn [indicators](#term:indicator-record) [57](#cite:57).
conditions: monthly, preliminary then revised; series IDs recorded for the refresh routine (t-3009)
